chapters.summary: Paul instructs Titus on how to appoint elders in the churches of Crete, and warns him to resist those who spread false teaching.
keyPoints: Paul calls himself a servant of God, sent for the sake of the faith of God's elect and their knowledge of the truth that leads to godliness.
An elder must be blameless, holding firmly to the true word, able both to exhort and to refute those who contradict it.
False teachers in Crete are greedy deceivers, and must be sharply rebuked so that they may become sound in the faith.
chapters.application: Today we should value the character of church leaders, hold fast to the truth, and boldly reject false teaching, building up the faith in love.

chapters.summary: Paul teaches Titus how to exhort believers of different ages and stations to live lives consistent with sound doctrine as they wait for the return of Christ.
keyPoints: He exhorts each group - older men, older women, young women, and young men - to conduct themselves properly.
He emphasizes that servants are to be obedient to their masters in everything, displaying the virtue of faithfulness.
He explains that the grace of God that brings salvation trains us to live godly lives as we wait for the blessed hope.
chapters.application: Let us bear witness to what we believe through our lives - whatever our age or station, may we glorify God in word and deed, and wait with hope for the Lord's return.

chapters.summary: Titus chapter 3 teaches believers to submit to those in authority, to treat others with gentleness, and to live out good works through God's grace and the renewing work of the Holy Spirit.
keyPoints: He reminds believers to submit to rulers and authorities, and to be ready to do every good work.
We too were once foolish and disobedient, but God saved us through regeneration and the renewing of the Holy Spirit.
Believers must be careful to devote themselves to good works, avoid foolish arguments, and after a warning, keep away from those who cause division.
chapters.application: We are not saved by our own righteousness, but by God's mercy. Let us treat others with gentleness, be eager to do good, and bear witness to Christ's salvation in our homes and workplaces.
